content.comment_body: We used [product_name] [article_no] together with [product_name] [product_name_operator_device] for a serial automation board, configuring IP addresses 192.168.1.40 for [product_name] and 192.168.1.41 for [product_name_operator_device]. Several customers reported loss of communication between [product_name] and [product_name_operator_device]. Upon investigation, we noticed that the [product_name_operator_device] IP unexpectedly reverted to factory settings, apparently following a power outage. This issue has occurred across multiple installations, so it appears to be a recurring bug rather than a defective single unit. It's intermittent, which makes diagnosis challenging. Has anyone else experienced this issue?
I regularly turn my [product_name] [article_no] and [product_name_operator_device] on and off and have never lost the settings of the [product_name_operator_device].

Please check the power supply in your setup and ensure that both [product_name] and [product_name_operator_device] are powered within the required specifications. Especially when power returns, it should quickly be within the proper range. I've had similar issues, but not with [product_name]. Previously, I used the same power supply for electronic boards and a large load. When powering up, if the voltage increased too slowly, the boards sometimes malfunctioned—causing configuration changes and memory loss. Using a regulated, independent power supply for the boards resolved it. Hope this is helpful.

analysis.insight_summary: A user describes an intermittent issue where the [product_name_operator_device]'s IP settings revert to default after a power outage, resulting in network communication problems on multiple installations. The problem is hard to replicate or diagnose but seems widespread. Other users have not seen this problem or suggest that unstable or slow-rising power supply can cause configuration or memory loss in similar devices.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the [product_name_operator_device] to maintain its network settings, particularly the IP address, after a power loss, and not return to factory defaults.
